text: There was a man among the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a Jewish leader.
He came to Jesus at night and said, 'Rabbi, we know you are a teacher who has come from God — no one could perform the signs you do unless God were with him.'
Jesus replied, 'Truly, truly I tell you — no one can see the kingdom of God without being born again.'
'How can a grown man be born?' Nicodemus asked. 'He can't climb back into his mother's womb and be born a second time, can he?'
Jesus answered, 'Truly, truly I tell you — no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit.'
'Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit.'
'Don't be surprised that I told you, you must all be born again.'
'The wind blows wherever it wants; you hear its sound, but you can't tell where it comes from or where it's going. It's the same with everyone born of the Spirit.'
'How is this even possible?' Nicodemus asked.
Jesus said, 'You are Israel's own teacher, and you don't understand this?'
'Truly, truly I tell you — we speak about what we know and testify about what we've seen, yet you people don't accept our testimony.'
'If I've told you about things on earth and you don't believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?'
'No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven — the Son of Man.'
'Just as Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the wilderness, the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way —'
'so that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life.'
'For this is how much God loved the world: he gave his one and only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but will have eternal life.'
'God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it, but so that the world would be saved through him.'
'Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already, for not believing in God's one and only Son.'
'And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, but people loved the darkness instead of the light, because their actions were evil.'
'Everyone who does evil hates the light and avoids it, for fear their actions will be exposed.'
'But whoever lives by the truth comes to the light, so it may be plainly seen that what they do has been done through God.'
After this Jesus and his disciples went out into the Judean countryside, where he spent time with them and baptized.
John, too, was baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there, and people kept coming to be baptized —
this was before John had been thrown into prison.
A dispute broke out between John's followers and a certain Jew over the practice of ceremonial washing.
So they came to John and said, 'Rabbi, the man who was with you on the far side of the Jordan, the one you testified about — look, he's baptizing now, and everyone is flocking to him.'
John answered, 'No one can receive anything unless it has been given to him from heaven.'
'You yourselves can testify that I said, I am not the Christ, but I have been sent ahead of him.'
'The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. The bridegroom's friend, standing nearby and listening for him, is overjoyed just to hear the bridegroom's voice. That joy is now mine, complete.'
'He must grow greater; I must grow smaller.'
'The one who comes from above is above everything; the one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks in earthly terms. The one who comes from heaven is above all.'
'He testifies to what he has seen and heard, and yet no one accepts his testimony.'
'Whoever does accept it has certified that God is truthful.'
'The one God sent speaks God's own words, since God gives the Spirit without limit.'
'The Father loves the Son and has put everything into his hands.'
'Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever refuses to believe in the Son will not see life — God's wrath remains on him instead.'
